html:
Seewoosagur Ramgoolam was the leader of the Mauritian independence movement and the first prime minister of Mauritius, from independence on 12 March 1968 until 1982.

The son of an indentured labourer who came through Aapravasi Ghat, he studied medicine in London and returned to lead the Labour Party, speaking for the Indo-Mauritian majority and the sugar workers.

Before independence, Britain detached the Chagos Islands from Mauritius, a deal he accepted and later regretted. In office he kept a democracy with regular elections in a mixed society of Hindus, Muslims, Creoles, Chinese and Franco-Mauritians, and began the move away from sugar. The main airport of Mauritius bears his name.
